EXPERIMENT 14
Implement OSPF Routing
1
Aim
To configure OSPF (Open Shortest Path First) routing on the routers and verify connec-
tivity using the routing table and ping commands.
2
Requirements
• Cisco Packet Tracer
• Four Cisco 2811 routers
• One PC
• Copper straight-through cable
• Serial DCE/DTE cables
3
Theory
OSPF (Open Shortest Path First) is a dynamic link-state routing protocol used by routers
to exchange information about the network topology and learn routes to remote networks.
OSPF uses cost as its routing metric and calculates the shortest path to a destination.
It uses Link-State Advertisements (LSAs) to exchange link-state information between
neighboring routers.
OSPF divides a network into areas. Area 0 is the backbone area. In this experiment,
all networks are configured in Area 0.
OSPF-learned routes are identified by the letter O in the routing table. The adminis-
trative distance of OSPF is 110.

Implement RIPv2 Routing
1
Aim
To configure RIPv2 (Routing Information Protocol Version 2) on the routers and verify
connectivity using the routing table and ping commands.
2
Requirements
• Cisco Packet Tracer
• Four Cisco 2811 routers
• One PC
• Copper straight-through cable
• Serial DCE/DTE cables
3
Theory
RIPv2 is a dynamic routing protocol used by routers to exchange routing information
and automatically learn routes to remote networks. RIP uses hop count as its routing
metric.
RIPv2 is enabled using the version 2 command. The no auto-summary command
disables automatic classful route summarization. The network command specifies the
networks on which RIP operates.
Routes learned through RIP are identified by the letter R in the routing table. RIP
has an administrative distance of 120.
